contradiction_resolution: NO CLAIM-LEVEL CONTRADICTION. contradicts_claim_ids is empty and the statement does not oppose CONJ-0001, THM-0001 through THM-0007, OBS-0001, or RED-0001. It is a structural/bookkeeping statement internal to the C66-COMP-RANK determinantal-and-excess computation, compatible with the packet's canonical geometric bottleneck and with the corroborated (6,6) findings cited below. INDEPENDENT DERIVATION (the load-bearing step, done by me, not delegated). Let pi: C -> B be smooth proper of genus six, L of relative degree six with pi_*L locally free of rank three and compatible with base change, AJ = P_B(pi_*L) in the lines/sub convention, p: C x_B AJ -> AJ, and D_univ the universal relative effective divisor. Then O(D_univ) = L_AJ tensor p^*M_univ with M_univ the tautological line on AJ. Applying Rp_* to 0 -> O -> O(D_univ) -> O_{D_univ}(D_univ) -> 0 gives 0 -> O_AJ -> p_*O(D_univ) -> p_*O_{D_univ}(D_univ) -> R^1 p_* O -> R^1 p_* O(D_univ) -> 0, the last term being right-exact because D_univ is affine over AJ. Here R^1 p_* O = pullback of R^1 pi_* O_C, which is the pullback of the tangent bundle of Pic^0 and hence the normal bundle of the section [L]; the middle connecting map is exactly the differential of the relative Abel map. Therefore coker(d a) = R^1 p_* O(D_univ) = R^1 p_*(L_AJ tensor p^*M_univ) = p^*(R^1 pi_* L) tensor M_univ by the projection formula, since M_univ is invertible on AJ. Fibrewise over a point of AJ above b in B this is H^1(C_b, L_b) tensor (a one-dimensional space), so geometric fibres are abstractly isomorphic to H^1(L_b) only after trivializing the M_univ fibre. Rank check: expected codimension of AJ in Div^6 is g = 6, actual relative codimension is 6 - 2 = 4, so the excess rank is 2 = h^1(L), consistent with the rank-two remark in FND-0129. Every clause of FND-0133 is thereby confirmed. PRIMARY-SOURCE ANCHORS. Kleiman, 'The Picard scheme' (arXiv:math/0504020; published as chapter 9 of Fundamental Algebraic Geometry, AMS Math. Surveys and Monographs 123, 2005): subsection 3.10 defines Q by the functorial isomorphism Hom(Q, N) = f_*(F tensor f^*N); Definition 3.12 introduces LinSys_{L/X/S}; Theorem 3.13 states that L := P(Q) represents LinSys_{L/X/S}, with P(Q) = Proj Sym(Q) in the Grothendieck convention, so its points are rank-one QUOTIENTS of Q and its tautological surjection is Q_L -> O(1); Exercise 3.14 states that there is a natural relative effective divisor W on X_L/L with O_{X_L}(W) = L_L tensor f_L^*O_L(1), i.e. the twist is by +O(1), not O(-1). When pi_*L is locally free and base-change compatible, Q = (pi_*L)^dual, so Kleiman's P(Q) is precisely the space of lines in pi_*L. The convention frame is EGA II (Grothendieck, Publ. Math. IHES 8, 1961), section 4.1 and 4.2.3, and Hartshorne II.7.11 to II.7.12. The identification of the Abel tangent map with the coboundary of 0 -> O_X -> O_X(D) -> N_D -> 0 is Kleiman Remark 5.18, citing Mumford, Lectures on Curves on an Algebraic Surface (1966), p. 165; ACGH volume I chapter IV sections 2 and 4 give the classical universal-divisor and Zariski-tangent-space treatment. The excess-bundle formalism E = g^*N / N with contribution c_{d-d'}(E) cap [W] is Fulton, Intersection Theory, section 6.3 (Thom-Porteous is section 14.4, not 17.4). SHARPENINGS THAT SHOULD BE RECORDED WITH THE PROMOTION. (1) The phrase 'untwisted Hodge-bundle isomorphism' is imprecise: the bundle in question is R^1 pi_* L, which is rank two and, by relative Serre duality with M := omega tensor L^dual of degree four, is (pi_*M)^dual; it is not the Hodge bundle pi_*omega_{C/B} of rank six. The correct reading of the clause is 'no untwisted identification with a bundle pulled back from B', and that reading is what the derivation supports. (2) The disjunct 'or prove it trivial' is provably unavailable on AJ itself and the finding can be strengthened accordingly: M_univ restricts to O(1) on each P^2 fibre, so c_1(M_univ) = xi is non-torsion; writing V = R^1 pi_* L, the rank-two excess bundle E = p^*V tensor M_univ has c_2(E) = c_2(V) + c_1(V) xi + xi^2, and p_*(c_1(V) xi + xi^2) = [B] since p_* xi = 0 and p_* xi^2 = [B]. Dropping the twist therefore perturbs the pushed-forward excess class by exactly [B], a definitively nonzero error. The hedge survives only for the OPEN ordered incidence: on the complement of the discriminant inside each P^2 fibre, the restriction of xi can become torsion in CH^1 with Q coefficients, so triviality there is a distinct statement that must be argued and may not be assumed. (3) The convention hazard is real and sharper than the finding states. It is not merely a sign on M_univ: read in the Grothendieck convention, 'P_B(pi_*L)' means Proj Sym(pi_*L), which parametrizes rank-one quotients of pi_*L and is NOT the relative linear system; the correct object is Proj Sym((pi_*L)^dual), which is how FND-0127 already writes it as P((pi_*L)^dual). Downstream artifacts should disambiguate the label, not just the twist sign. (4) Generality: as with FND-0096, the twist identification transports verbatim to any (g,n) and any L with locally free base-change-compatible pushforward; only excess rank two is (6,6)-specific. (5) Existence hypotheses: writing AJ as a projective bundle at all presupposes constant h^0(L), which is the FND-0047 / FND-0107 / FND-0131 hypothesis; over nonreduced or h^0-jumping bases the FND-0107 Abel-Jacobi fibre model must be used and the twist formula then holds on the locus where the projective-bundle model is valid. On a stack base the FND-0127 smooth-atlas descent line is required. (6) 'Globally' is correct in the sense 'as an isomorphism of sheaves on all of AJ (and on its etale cover)', not 'descends to B'. DISTINCTNESS AND MERGE. Nearest sibling is FND-0129, which concerns the same excess square but fixes the typing of the zero section e: B -> Pic^0 and the coker-versus-dual choice, noting that c_2 agrees in rank two. FND-0133 supplies the global identification of that cokernel including the tautological twist that FND-0129 leaves unnamed; the two are complementary and neither subsumes the other, so they should not be merged. Distinct from FND-0122, whose cokernel is the CE evaluation cokernel of phi_5, Serre-dual to H^0 of a degree-zero line bundle and of generic rank at most one - conflating that with this rank-two excess cokernel is exactly the kind of error this finding guards against. Distinct from FND-0096 (Fitting ideal of the evaluation cokernel over Pic^0), from FND-0107 / FND-0047 / FND-0131 (representability and base change), and from FND-0127 (base scope).
